newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - June 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - June 18.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents.
-- WATCHDOG SETS CONDITIONS FOR BSKYB DIGITAL TV ROLE

The Independent Television Commission has ruled that British Sky Broadcasting must drop its equity stake in one of the contenders to launch digital television in the country for fear the company would concentrate too much power in too few hands. The ITC warns that if no such move is made, the consortium, which also includes Carlton Communications and Granada Group, will be ruled out of the contest.
-- COMPANIES HIT AT CODE BREAK PLAN

The UK Business Software Alliance and the British Interactive Media Association have lashed out against government proposals to permit security services to decipher coded electronic messages from terrorists and drug barons, declaring they are 'unworkable, unneeded and frankly unacceptable'. The electronic groups warn that the proposals open the way for the regulatory net to be spread far wider than reasonable, thus stifling innovation.
-- ADVERTISING SPENDING HITS RECORD 12 BILLION STERLING

The Advertising Association has revealed that British spending on advertisements in 1996 amounted to 11.99 billion sterling, compared with 10.98 billion the year before. Direct mail saw the largest increase, accounting for 12 percent of total advertising compared with 10 percent in 1995. Television advertising came to 3.33 billion sterling of the total and classified press advertisements totalled to 2.77 billion sterling.
-- MICROSOFT OUTLINES 60M STERLING INVESTMENT IN CAMBRIDGE

US software giant Microsoft has made plans to invest ten million sterling into high-tech start-ups in the Cambridge area, as well as 50 million sterling into the construction of a new computer science research laboratory in conjunction with the university. Microsoft's chief technology officer Nathan Myhrvoid said the lab will seek to 'stimulate a lot of entrepreneurial activity' in the area, looking to attain profit through venture investments.
-- NATWEST SHARES FALL ON BROKERS' FORECASTS

Shares in National Westminster Bank fell again on Tuesday, as stockbrokers reacted to a profits warning from the group by downgrading the shares. Analysts have reduced their full-year forecasts for NatWest to between 1.72bn stg and 1.79bn stg, as opposed to the expected 2.1bn stg. On Monday, the resignation of Martin Owen from his position as marketing chief executive was accompanied by the announcement that a review was ongoing into NatWest's markets operations and that first half profits would be 'significantly lower than for the same period last year'.
-- GENCOR CLOSE TO $7BN LONDON LISTING

Analysts predict that South Africa's second-largest mining group, Gencor, is close to the announcement of a London listing for its aluminum, coal and metals business, valued at 4.2bn stg. When it occurs, the demerger will signal the culmination of Gencor's transformation into an international metals group, while demonstrating that South Africa is committed to a relaxation of exchange controls. The demerger is also expected to raise about one billion stg to fund projects in Africa, Australia, Colombia and Venezuela.
-- MOUNTING LOSSES FAIL TO DIM ATLANTIC TELECOM'S PROMISE

Scottish telecoms company Atlantic Telecom has released figures for the year to March 31 which show the group has fallen deeper into debt, with pre-tax losses of 2.85m stg compared with 812,000 the year before. Atlantic, currently pioneering wireless telephony for the Glasgow area, made a one million stg provision for the sale or closure of its remaining narrow band cable activities. Chairman Graham Duncan said the results were better than expected, as 12 percent of sales emanated from telephony.
-- DEMERGER COSTS KEEP REBUS TO 6.1M STG

The former computer arm of insurer CE Heath, Rebus Group, has reported pre-tax and pre-exceptional profits of 6.1m stg, compared to 6.5m stg the year before. Rebus chief executive Peter Presland attributed the smaller profit to a 1.3m stg rise in costs as a result of the demerger. Operating profits at the group were up 30 percent to 9.3m stg, as Rebus spent 2m stg on development of new businesses.
-- HAZLEWOOD CONTINUES RECOVERY AND FEASTS ON CONVENIENCE FOODS

Having overcome the effects of the BSE crisis, Hazlewood Foods has reported a nine percent rise in underlying profits in the second half to 37m stg. Hazlewood has revealed that it sold its Dutch potato products subsidiary for 45m stg, moving away from commodity businesses in an effort to concentrate more on convenience foods. Pre-tax profits at the group fell slightly to 32.3m stg, with group sales totalling 766m stg and operating profits up nine percent to 44m stg.
-- EMI FINALISES 'CASH BACK' PLAN

The EMI record company has released the final details of a capital return scheme which will see 499.1m stg given back to shareholders. The return scheme, funded by debt and seen by some as an attempt to bolster shares as takeover rumours have ended, will involve issuing a B share worth 114.5p to investors for each ordinary share already held and can be redeemed from July 22 to August 19.
